## Read in the Dataset

```{r}
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse)
bike_data <- read_csv("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale=locale(encoding="latin1"))
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis

- Check missing values

```{r}
#check each column for missing values
bike_data |> summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.x))))
```

- Convert date to a date object

```{r}
library(lubridate)
bike_data <- bike_data |> mutate(Date = lubridate::dmy(Date))

head(bike_data)
```

- Change categorical variables to factors

```{r}
#change categorical variables to factors
bike_data <- bike_data |> mutate(Seasons = as.factor(Seasons),
                                 Holiday = as.factor(Holiday),
                                `Functioning Day` = as.factor(`Functioning Day`))

head(bike_data)
```

- Change column names to be more readable

```{r}
bike_data <- bike_data |> rename(date = Date,
                                             rented_bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
                                             hour = Hour,
                                             temperature = `Temperature(°C)`,
                                             humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
                                             wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
                                             visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
                                             dew_point_temperature = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
                                             solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
                                             rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
                                             snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
                                             seasons = Seasons,
                                             holiday = Holiday,
                                             functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
)

head(bike_data)
```

- Get the summary data for bike counts

```{r}
bike_data |> summarise(
  mean_bikes = mean(rented_bike_count),
  median_bikes = median(rented_bike_count),
  max_bikes = max(rented_bike_count),
  min_bikes = min(rented_bike_count)
)
```

- Since no bikes are rented on non functioning days lets remove those observations

```{r}
bike_data <- bike_data |> filter(!functioning_day == 'No')

head(bike_data)
```

- Lets gets the summarized daily data

```{r}
daily_bike <- bike_data |> group_by(date,seasons,holiday) |>
  summarise(
    bike_count = sum(rented_bike_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    temperature = mean(temperature),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    windspeed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dewpoint_temp = mean(dew_point_temperature),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
head(daily_bike)
dim(daily_bike)
```

## Split the Data

- Lets split the data for testing and training with 75% of observations in training and the rest for testing. The data is split with the strata argument as seasons.

```{r}
library(tidymodels)

set.seed(10)
bike_split <- initial_split(daily_bike, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)
bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

dim(bike_train)
dim(bike_test)
```

- Now lets create a 10 fold split for cross validation on the training data

```{r}
bike_10_fold <- vfold_cv(bike_train, 10)

bike_10_fold
```

## Fitting MLR Models

- For the first recipe

```{r}
recipe_1 <- recipe(bike_count ~ ., data = bike_train) |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |> 
  step_mutate(
    day_type = as.factor(ifelse(date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),"weekend","weekday" ))
  ) |>
  step_rm(date,date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type)

recipe_1
```

- Second recipe

```{r}
recipe_2 <- recipe(bike_count ~ ., data = bike_train) |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |> 
  step_mutate(
    day_type = as.factor(ifelse(date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),"weekend","weekday" ))
  ) |>
  step_rm(date,date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  step_interact(~starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") +
                  starts_with("seasons_"):temperature +
                  temperature:rainfall)

recipe_2


```

- Third Recipe

```{r}
recipe_3 <- recipe(bike_count ~ ., data = bike_train) |>
  step_date(date, features = "dow") |> 
  step_mutate(
    day_type = as.factor(ifelse(date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),"weekend","weekday" ))
  ) |>
  step_rm(date,date_dow) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  step_interact(~starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") +
                  starts_with("seasons_"):temperature +
                  temperature:rainfall) |>
  step_mutate(quad_temp = temperature^2,
              quad_humid = humidity^2)



recipe_3
```

## Fitting the Model

- Take all the recipes and create workflows with the engine as linear model. Then combine the results of the fit using CV.

```{r}
linear_model <- linear_reg()|> set_engine("lm")

bike_wfl_1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe_1) |>
  add_model(linear_model)

bike_wfl_2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe_2) |>
  add_model(linear_model)

bike_wfl_3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe_3) |>
  add_model(linear_model)


workflows_list <- list(
  recipe_1 = bike_wfl_1,
  recipe_2 = bike_wfl_2,
  recipe_3 = bike_wfl_3
)
model_results <- bind_rows(
  fit_resamples(bike_wfl_1, bike_10_fold) |> collect_metrics() |> mutate(model = "recipe_1"),
  fit_resamples(bike_wfl_2, bike_10_fold) |> collect_metrics() |> mutate(model = "recipe_2"),
  fit_resamples(bike_wfl_3, bike_10_fold) |> collect_metrics() |> mutate(model = "recipe_3")
)
model_results
```

- Select the best model with the smallest rmse and fit using the whole dataset

```{r}

best_model <- model_results |> filter(.metric == "rmse") |> arrange(mean) |> slice(1)


last_mlr <- last_fit(workflows_list[[best_model$model]], bike_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse,mae)) 

final_model <- last_mlr |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> tidy()
final_model
```

- Now lets select the best for the regression tree model

```{r}
library(tidymodels)
library(rpart.plot)
tune_spec <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

tree_grid <- grid_regular(cost_complexity(),
                          tree_depth(),
                          levels =5)
tree_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe_1) |>
  add_model(tune_spec)

tree_res <- tree_wf |> tune_grid(resamples = bike_10_fold, grid = tree_grid, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

best_tree <- select_best(tree_res, metric = "rmse")
tree_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(tree_wf, best_tree)
final_tree <- fit(tree_final_wf, bike_train)

```

- find the best bagged tree model and fit

```{r}
library(baguette)
bag_spec <- bag_tree(cost_complexity = tune(),
                     tree_depth = tune()) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

bag_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(recipe_1) |>
  add_model(bag_spec)

bag_res <- bag_wf |> tune_grid(resamples = bike_10_fold, grid = tree_grid, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

best_bag <- select_best(bag_res, metric = "rmse")
bag_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(bag_wf, best_bag)
final_bag <- fit(bag_final_wf, bike_train)

```

- Find the best random forest model and fit

```{r}
library(ranger)
library(vip)
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 1000) |>
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") |>
  set_mode("regression")

rf_wf <- workflow() |>
  add_model(rf_spec) |>
  add_recipe(recipe_1)

# grid for all features
rf_grid <- grid_regular(mtry(range = c(1,13)), min_n(), levels = 5)
rf_res <-rf_wf |>
  tune_grid(resamples = bike_10_fold, grid = rf_grid, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

best_rf <- select_best(rf_res, metric = "rmse")
rf_final_wf <- finalize_workflow(rf_wf, best_rf)
final_rf <- fit(rf_final_wf, bike_train)
```

## Model Testing

- Now it is time to use the models that we made on the test data set to see which one performed the best

```{r}

last_tree <- last_fit(tree_final_wf, bike_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
last_bag <- last_fit(bag_final_wf, bike_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))
last_rf <- last_fit(rf_final_wf, bike_split, metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae))

test_results <- bind_rows(
  collect_metrics(last_mlr) |> mutate(model = "MLR"),
  collect_metrics(last_bag) |> mutate(model = "Bagged Tree"),
  collect_metrics(last_tree) |> mutate(model = "Regression Tree"),
  collect_metrics(last_rf) |> mutate(model = "Random Forest")
)

test_results |> select(model, .metric, .estimate) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) |> arrange(rmse, mae)
```

## Model Summaries

```{r}
#extract workflow to help in getting summaries
final_mlr  <- extract_workflow(last_mlr)
final_tree <- extract_workflow(last_tree)
final_bag  <- extract_workflow(last_bag)
final_rf   <- extract_workflow(last_rf)


#final coefficient table for MLR
final_mlr |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> tidy()

#regression tree plot
final_tree |> extract_fit_engine() |> rpart.plot(roundint = FALSE)


#Bagged tree variable importance plot


#Random Forest variable importance plot
final_rf |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> vip()

#final fit on the best model which is the tuned random forest model
final_best_model <- fit(rf_final_wf, daily_bike)
final_best_model
```
